meta.title: Timeline
meta.description: A time-axis infrastructure system. Ruler with zoom-aware ticks, synchronized track lanes, a draggable playhead, and time↔pixel math. Consumer owns the track content — clips, keyframes, waveforms, events.

blocks.content: Building a timeline UI always fails the same way. The ruler stops making sense after zooming. The playhead drifts from the ruler after scrolling. Zooming jumps to the wrong position instead of anchoring to the cursor. The track headers don't stay visible while scrolling horizontally.

The system owns the time infrastructure and nothing else. TimelineRoot manages time state, zoom, and scroll. TimelineRuler calculates tick intervals that stay readable at any zoom level. TimelineTrack provides synchronized track lanes with sticky headers. TimelineClip and TimelineKeyframe position consumer content at any time range or point. What goes inside a track — video clips, animation keyframes, audio waveforms, game events — is always the consumer's concern.

blocks.title: The system handles three hard problems
blocks.content: 1. Ruler ticks: the interval adjusts so ticks are always at least 60px apart, switching from milliseconds to seconds to minutes as you zoom out. 2. Zoom anchoring: zooming in/out keeps the time under your cursor fixed, not the start of the timeline. 3. Scroll sync: the ruler and all track lanes share a single scroll position via CSS sticky, with no JavaScript mirroring.
Four tracks: Video, Audio, Text, Effects. Click the ruler to scrub. Use the zoom buttons or Ctrl+scroll to zoom. Press play to animate the playhead.

Five property tracks with keyframe markers: X Position, Y Position, Rotation, Scale, Opacity. Scrub the playhead and watch the preview box update in real time — the system provides the time infrastructure, the consumer handles the interpolation.
Wrap your tracks in TimelineRoot with a duration. Add TimelineTrack for each lane. Use TimelineClip or TimelineKeyframe to position consumer content at specific times.

blocks.content: TimelineClip positions children absolutely within a track at a start–end time range. TimelineKeyframe positions a point marker at a single time. Both read zoom from context — no manual pixel calculation needed.

blocks.title: Content is always yours
blocks.content: TimelineClip and TimelineKeyframe are positioning helpers only. They set left and width via the zoom factor from context. What renders inside — the clip label, waveform visualization, color coding — is your component.

Ctrl+scroll (or Cmd+scroll on Mac) zooms anchored to the cursor position. Zoom buttons step by ×1.4 and ×0.7. Scroll horizontally with the trackpad or scrollbar. All zoom and scroll state is in TimelineRoot — useTimeline exposes it for custom controls.
